terms.definition: The cross-functional operational framework and cultural practice that brings financial accountability, cost transparency, and business value optimization to AI and machine learning workloads.
The technical discipline of measuring, managing, governing, and optimizing token consumption, context windows, model routing, and prompt efficiency across generative AI applications.
The basic atomic unit of text, code, or multimodal prompt data sent to an LLM for inference, metered and billed by providers according to model-specific rates.

The generated completion unit returned by a model (including internal chain-of-thought or reasoning tokens), typically billed at a 3x to 5x higher rate than input tokens due to autoregressive compute demands.
An inference optimization where prefix Key-Value (KV) cache states are stored in accelerator memory across requests, reducing latency and discounting input token billing by 50% to 90%.
The latency interval between submitting an inference request and receiving the first generated token, dominated by prompt ingestion, prefill compute, and network transmission.
The throughput speed at which an inference engine or model generates completion tokens once decoding has begun, reflecting decoding efficiency and memory bandwidth.
A cloud pricing model where an organization reserves dedicated GPU capacity or throughput units for a fixed hourly or annual fee, offering guaranteed availability and consistent latency.
An asynchronous processing endpoint provided by model vendors that processes non-real-time requests (such as evaluations, embeddings, and batch summarization) within 24 hours at a 50% cost discount.
Techniques such as semantic pruning, summarization of dialogue history, and selective retrieval designed to minimize prompt tokens sent to an LLM without degrading context fidelity.
An architectural pattern where incoming prompts are classified by complexity, intent, or latency needs and dynamically routed to the most cost-effective model tier capable of completing the task.
A centralized reverse proxy positioned between client applications and model providers to enforce rate limits, authentication, unified telemetry, prompt caching, circuit breaking, and fallbacks.

Showback provides financial visibility and reporting to consuming teams without transferring internal budget, whereas Chargeback directly debits consuming cost centers for their measured AI consumption.
Financial metrics that evaluate AI expenditure relative to direct business outcomes, such as cost per active user, cost per resolved customer inquiry, or cost per accepted code commit.
Industry-standard attribute and metric naming schemas established by OpenTelemetry (under gen_ai.*) that ensure observability and cost attribution data remain consistent across multiple providers.

Compressing model weights from full precision (FP16 or BF16) to lower bit precision (such as FP8, INT8, or INT4), drastically reducing GPU VRAM requirements and hosting costs with minimal quality degradation.

An inference engine serving technique that dynamically schedules and batches incoming requests at the token level rather than request level, maximizing GPU compute saturation and driving down unit cost.
An automated stability control that interrupts execution or drops downstream requests when predefined cost thresholds, error rates, or recursive loop depths are detected in autonomous agents.
FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification; an open standard defining cloud and AI consumption billing columns, standardizing ChargeType, ConsumedQuantity, and EffectiveCost across multi-cloud ledgers.
Internal chain-of-thought tokens produced during test-time compute by reasoning models (such as o1 or DeepSeek-R1) to plan and evaluate intermediate steps, billed as billable output tokens.
A memory allocation algorithm inspired by OS virtual memory that partitions KV-cache tensors into non-contiguous physical memory blocks, eliminating internal fragmentation in LLM serving engines.
